quotes.speaker: Tyler Herro
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyler Herro on the team's inability to sustain defensive intensity
quotes.excerpt: we're trying to sustain our game for 48 minutes. We've seen it in pockets
quotes.quote: We're trying to sustain our game for 48 minutes. We've seen it in pockets, but in the second half, we didn't really crash the glass much, and that was part of why they were able to get out in transition. We got to lose, I think, 16 less possessions than them. It's tough to beat anyone with 16 less possessions.
quotes.social_post: Tyler Herro says the team is struggling to sustain defensive intensity for 48 minutes. He noted that losing the possession battle by 16 makes it very tough to beat anyone.

structured.context: Tyler Herro discusses the team's struggles with defensive intensity and rebounding during a postgame media availability.

quotes.speaker: Tyler Herro
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyler Herro on the team's late-game execution and defensive struggles
quotes.excerpt: I would say Boston is probably the first crunch time to clutch minutes
quotes.quote: I would say Boston is probably the first crunch time to clutch minutes, however you want to look at a late type fourth quarter for you guys tonight. Kind of the early fourth before it stretched out you guys kind of had more chances. What have you seen these last couple of games, last couple minutes execution-wise which is just trying to get to your stuff if there isn't a second chance or if there isn't a layup? I think defensively, in the first half again we were getting stops. Second half they were comfortable, they were able to score, so now we're taking it out every single time and now we're playing against a set defense. I think the more we get stops and get in transition we can run. They're a really good defensive team, they're long, they play physical, so we get stops, we can run in transition and then we're able to not go against a set defense every time.
quotes.social_post: Tyler Herro on the team's late game struggles against Boston. He says the team needs to get more stops to avoid playing against a set defense every time down the floor.

structured.context: Tyler Herro explains the team's difficulty in executing against Boston's set defense when failing to generate transition opportunities.

quotes.speaker: Tyler Herro
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyler Herro on maintaining team composure during scoring runs
quotes.excerpt: figuring out a way to rally around each other even when shots aren't falling
quotes.quote: I think just staying, obviously the best part of the game are runs, so they're going to go on runs, we're going to go on runs, but figuring out a way to rally around each other even when shots aren't falling. You have to play defense, stick to our our head is defensively, and that's kind of been the theme for us. It's a theme league-wide that when teams are making shots, they don't defend, and the best teams in this league do that. So finding ways to continue to play our game offensively, shots may not be going in, but we still got to defend even if shots aren't falling.
quotes.social_post: Tyler Herro says the theme for the team is to keep defending even when shots are not falling. He believes the best teams in the league do not let their offense dictate their defensive effort.

structured.context: Tyler Herro emphasizes the importance of maintaining defensive focus even when the team is struggling to make shots.

quotes.speaker: Tyler Herro
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyler Herro on the team's patience during a difficult start
quotes.excerpt: it's a process. We've been saying this since the trade, this isn't a thing that happens overnight
quotes.quote: It's a process. We've been saying this since the trade, this isn't a thing that happens overnight. We've been in a lot of these games, and I think we've played eight to nine games, we should have won five of them. The other two or three we were obviously got blown out, but five of the eight I feel like we were in position to win all of them. Continuing to just go to that process, we'll start winning games, so I'm not worried.
quotes.social_post: Tyler Herro remains confident despite the team's slow start. He says they have been in position to win five of their first eight games and that the team is just trusting the process.

structured.context: Tyler Herro reflects on the team's early season performance and patience following a recent trade.

quotes.speaker: Tyler Herro
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyler Herro on the growth and potential of teammate Jaime Jaquez Jr.
quotes.excerpt: I love Jaime. He's my rook. I love seeing his growth
quotes.quote: I love Jaime. He's my rook. I love seeing his growth. He's going to continue to be one of the better players on this team, but one of the better players in the league as he continues to grow. So I'm excited to just see how he grows, and things with the rookies are, it's not like this, it's a little bumpy, but he's a hard worker and he's going to continue to get better every day.
quotes.social_post: Tyler Herro is high on the potential of teammate Jaime Jaquez Jr. calling him a hard worker who is going to continue to be one of the better players in the league.

structured.context: Tyler Herro praises the work ethic and growth of his teammate Jaime Jaquez Jr.
